subject: Hosted API renewal + surge buffer onramp; dynamic rateband proposal
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@streamly.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@streamly.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal conversation + expected Q4 surge

Hi Irene,

Quick note as our contract renewal window approaches — Streamly expects a material product push in Q4 (holiday marketing + two new integrations). We ran last quarter at ~950k tokens/month and project up to 3.2M tokens/month at peak over six weeks.

We want to avoid throttling and keep latency SLOs intact, so looking to: 1) increase our monthly hosted commit for the renewal term, 2) add a defined surge buffer (temporary overage pool), and 3) understand how rate bands would shift as we step through tiers.

Can Redwood share a recommended commit + surge construct (monthly baseline, burst allocation, soft-throttle triggers) and a sense of unit pricing for the different tiers? Also, any minimum term or notice windows to enable a committed uplift?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call this week.

—Sam
Sam Patel
Head of Platform
Streamly AI
sam.patel@streamly.ai
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@streamly.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + expected Q4 surge

Hi Sam — thanks for the heads up and congrats on the product push. We can definitely support a structured uplift that preserves latency and provides predictable economics. I pulled Karthik in (sales) for pricing and Vanessa for operations/throughput.

High-level proposal (attached: 2026-Streamly-Proposal-v2.pdf + commit calculator):
- Baseline commit: 1.5M tokens/month (12-month term)
- Surge buffer: additional 1.5M token pool usable for up to 6 weeks (billed at a reduced burst rate, not the baseline rate)
- Dynamic rateband step: three stair-step tiers (<=1.5M, 1.5M–3.0M, >3.0M) with per-token pricing that softens as you commit higher baseline; automatic soft-throttle threshold at 120% of baseline unless surge buffer elected

Operational notes:
- We can activate baseline uplifts within 5 business days of signature for US regions.
- If you prefer a temporary (90-day) committed uplift rather than full-term step, we can structure a priced addendum.

Karthik — can you attach a simple committed + burst pricing table and confirm DocuSign cadence? Vanessa — can Ops pre-warm any cache/batching config for their expected distributions?

If it's helpful, propose a call Thursday 10am PT.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@streamly.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + expected Q4 surge

Sam — attaching the commit calculator we discussed (streamly-commit-calculator.xlsx) and summarizing pricing options inline for speed: 

Option A — 12m baseline (recommended)
- Baseline: 1.5M tokens/mo @ $0.0018/token
- Surge pool: 1.5M tokens (6-week window) billed at $0.0022/token when consumed
- Effective blended price at 3.0M steady usage: ~$0.00195/token

Option B — 3m limited-term uplift (90 days)
- Baseline: 1.5M tokens/mo @ $0.0019/token
- Temporary committed uplift: +1.5M tokens/mo (90 days) @ $0.0020/token (after 90 days, reverts unless extended)

Operational controls:
- Soft-throttle at 120% of baseline to prevent noisy neighbor effects (alerts + 10 min grace + automated fallback to a compatible lower-capacity model if you opt in)
- Prefix caching and KV warm-up runbook will be prioritized; Vanessa — Ops can start a dry-run the week before launch.

DocuSign & timeline:
- We can issue an amendment with Option A within 48 hours; standard turnaround for a countersigned DocuSign is 2–4 business days. HubSpot deal DL-7821-STRM will be updated with the amendment link.

Sam — if you confirm Option A, I’ll push the amendment and request signature. If you'd rather keep flexibility, Option B gives a temporary uplift but at slightly higher unit costs.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Revenue
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@streamly.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@streamly.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation + expected Q4 surge

Karthik / Irene — thanks, this is helpful. We reviewed Option A internally and prefer the 12m baseline + surge buffer approach. A couple of small asks before we sign: 

1) Can the surge pool be split into two windows (4 weeks at launch + 2 weeks later) rather than a single contiguous 6-week window? We have two campaigns staggered in Nov and Dec.
2) Can you add a clause to the amendment that allows one speed-limited testbed on a smaller model variant in case we hit unforeseen latency regressions (auto-failover path)?

Assuming yes to both, we are ready for the amendment and will route for signature; please send DocuSign and we’ll aim for counter-sign within 48 hours.
